description: Four-row by three-column EBSD composite (every panel carries a 100 μm scale bar) showing fatigue crack paths at a stress amplitude of 225 MPa for four Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C (wt%) conditions: ST (a-c), 550-6 (d-f), 600-6 (g-i) and 650-6 (j-l). Column 1 (a,d,g,j) shows band-contrast (BC) maps with inverse-pole-figure (IPF) colouring superimposed; the IPF legend in (j) contains a 001/101/111 colour triangle labelled "IPF Coloring", "Iron fcc Fe" and Z0. Column 2 (b,e,h,k) shows kernel average misorientation (KAM) maps, with a blue-to-red "Legend for kernel average misorientation" colour bar in (k). Column 3 (c,f,i,l) shows Schmid factor maps, with the legend "Schmid Factor (111)<110>" in (l). Cracks appear as dark traces in the BC maps and as a bright white path in the SF maps, most clearly in (i) and (l). All KAM panels are dominated by dark blue low-misorientation matrix with bright green/yellow bands decorating grain boundaries and the crack path; (b) is the brightest, (e) and (h) appear more diffuse, and (k) shows discrete localized hot spots marked by red arrows. Taken together the panels argue that cracks advance transgranularly along slip bands in every condition, while path tortuosity, branching and grain-boundary strain localization differ systematically with κ-carbide precipitation state.

subfigures.description: BC + IPF superimposed EBSD map of the ST sample: equiaxed austenite grains in a wide spread of IPF colours (red, green, blue, purple, yellow), with a dark band-contrast trace running along the upper-left region; 100 μm scale bar.

KAM map of ST: predominantly dark blue low-misorientation matrix crossed by intensified bright green/yellow lines along grain boundaries and along the crack path; visually the brightest KAM panel of the four.
Schmid factor map of ST: grains coloured over a broad SF range (red through yellow to green/blue), with a faint bright line tracing the crack; 100 μm scale bar.
BC + IPF superimposed map of the 550-6 sample: large coloured grains with a dark crack trace crossing the map; 100 μm scale bar.
KAM map of 550-6: dark blue matrix with dimmer, more diffuse green misorientation bands than in (b), following grain boundaries and the crack path.
Schmid factor map of 550-6: grain-scale SF colouring (red/orange/green) with a small bright spot marking a local feature; 100 μm scale bar.
BC + IPF superimposed map of 600-6: multi-coloured grains with a dark crack trace running across the upper-middle portion.
KAM map of 600-6: mostly dark blue with bright green segments concentrated along the crack path and selected grain boundaries; a few bright speckles in the matrix.
Schmid factor map of 600-6: grains in red/orange/green tones with a clearly visible bright white crack line running diagonally across the panel.
BC + IPF superimposed map of 650-6: coloured grains with a dark crack trace; this panel also hosts the IPF colour triangle legend (001/101/111, 'IPF Coloring', 'Iron fcc Fe', Z0).

KAM map of 650-6: dark blue matrix with a bright green crack path and discrete localized hot spots indicated by two red arrows; contains the 'Legend for kernel average misorientation' colour bar (numeric limits unreadable).
Schmid factor map of 650-6: red/orange grain colouring with a bright white crack path and red arrows pointing to features along the path; contains the legend 'Schmid Factor (111)<110>'.

observations.observation: The figure is a 4×3 EBSD composite: rows correspond to samples ST (a-c), 550-6 (d-f), 600-6 (g-i) and 650-6 (j-l), columns to BC+IPF superimposed maps (a,d,g,j), KAM maps (b,e,h,k) and SF maps (c,f,i,l).
Every one of the twelve EBSD panels carries a 100 μm scale bar in its lower-right corner.
The KAM panels (b,e,h,k) consist of a dark blue low-misorientation matrix with bright green/yellow bands that decorate grain boundaries and the crack path rather than filling whole grains.
Two red arrows in panel (k) mark discrete localized KAM 'hot spots' along a grain boundary in the 650-6 sample.
Red arrows also appear in the 650-6 SF map (l), pointing at features along the crack path.
The IPF colouring legend printed in panel (j) shows a 001/101/111 colour triangle labelled 'IPF Coloring', 'Iron fcc Fe' and Z0, indicating the inverse pole figure refers to the fcc austenite phase.
The SF map legend in (l) is printed as 'Schmid Factor (111)<110>', i.e. the Schmid factor is resolved for {111}<110> slip in the fcc austenite.

The caption states that the BC and IPF superimposed maps reveal cracks in all four samples propagating along slip bands in a transgranular mode, consistent with crack advance along favorably oriented {111} slip planes in FCC alloys.

The caption states that the ST sample shows a relatively straight crack path within large austenite grains, whereas the aged samples 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6 show greater path tortuosity and frequent microbranching.

The caption reports that the ST sample has the highest KAM intensity and steepest gradients at boundaries, 550-6 and especially 600-6 show more moderate and diffuse KAM levels, and 650-6 again shows localized KAM hot spots at grain boundaries decorated with intergranular κ-carbides.
The citing text states that cracks nucleate in 'hard-oriented' grains (low SF) and propagate into adjacent 'soft-oriented' grains (high SF), which provides a low-energy path for crack advancement.

The citing text states that the EBSD step size and spatial resolution cannot resolve individual nanoscale intragranular κ-carbides, so no one-to-one correspondence between single precipitates and local crack deflections can be established.
The citing text states that the EBSD maps were acquired adjacent to the main cracks in samples tested at a stress amplitude of 225 MPa.

The citing text attributes the increased crack branching and deflection in the aged samples to intragranular κ-carbides acting as nanoscale obstacles that redistribute the crack-tip stress field and activate multiple slip systems.

panel (l): numeric values of the Schmid factor colour bar are illegible
panel (j): the IPF legend text beyond 'IPF Coloring'/'Iron fcc Fe'/'Z0' and the small phase label are only partially readable
